subject: On-prem VPC activation: EU/APAC routing constraints and handoff
messages:
From: Evan Liu <evan.liu@acme-payments.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-payments.com>, Acme Payments Infra <infra@acme-payments.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: On-prem activation window and routing constraints

Connor — thanks again for the call today. We're preparing the on-prem/VPC activation for our EU tenant and need to lock the plan for how failover to APAC standby will be handled without crossing residency boundaries. Two specific asks: 

1) Can Redwood confirm that during a failover/evacuation the control-plane handoff can be performed with no user-data egress to non-EU regions? We need a statement we can pass to our legal/compliance team.

2) We have an existing edge in APAC that receives some egress for latency-sensitive reads. For the warm-standby plan, what networking changes (BGP prep, prefix limits, ACLs) do you need on our side? We included a network diagram (attached) and hope you can annotate.

Attachment: acme_mip_network_diagram_v2.pdf (diagram, 2 pages)

Thanks — Evan
Evan Liu
Director, Platform Engineering | Acme Payments

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-payments.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem activation window and routing constraints

Evan — thanks for the clear asks, and for the diagram. I'm looping in our residency leads and the operations PM so we can give a concise handoff plan. High level answers up front:

- Control-plane handoff can be executed entirely within the EU; we will not route user payloads to APAC during the control-plane transition. We will, however, need temporary routing for telemetry and some health checks depending on the activation mode — we can route those to a scrubbed endpoint.

- For warm-standby reads served from APAC, we need the customer to explicitly opt-in to geo-egress for those read-only cache layers; that will be a separate config during cutover. ACLs/BGP prep items are listed in the attached checklist.

Next steps: I'll get a short, compliance-ready statement from Hannah and a proposed cutover runbook from Vivek by EOD tomorrow. Steph, please confirm whether the canary will include prefix announcements or just ACL toggles.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-12T13:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem activation window and routing constraints

Connor / team — draft compliance statement below (will refine to legal language if Acme requires):

"Redwood Inference confirms that during activation and any planned failover from EU primary to APAC warm-standby, no customer-created user data payloads (requests or stored content) will be sent to APAC regions unless explicitly configured by the customer for geo-egress read-only behavior. Control-plane messages required for orchestration (health checks, audit events) will be limited to metadata-only endpoints and, where feasible, routed via EU-resident collectors. Any telemetry that must leave EU will be minimized and masked per our data handling policy."

We should attach a short appendix describing the telemetry classes that may require temporary non-EU egress and mitigation controls (sampling, masking, retention < 24h). I've attached the residency checklist that maps to these items.

Attachment: redwood-residency-checklist.xlsx (residency checklist, 1 sheet)

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Trust & Compliance | Redwood Inference

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-payments.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-13T08:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem activation window and routing constraints

Thanks — that draft statement is really helpful. A couple of clarifying questions from compliance: 

- When you say "control-plane messages required for orchestration", can you list the specific protocols/ports (e.g., TCP 9443 for control API; prometheus metrics scrape) so our network team can produce a whitelist during the activation window?

- For the APAC read-only opt-in, will that require BGP announcements from our colo or just a ref to our existing CDN/edge? We want to avoid changing our upstream announcements if possible.

If you can provide port/protocols and a minimal checklist (network-side tasks), we can route that to our infra and legal for signoff.

Priya
Priya Shah
Head of Compliance | Acme Payments

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-payments.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Steph Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-14T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem activation window and routing constraints

Priya — quick answers and minimal actionable checklist below. We'll put a formal runbook into the linked Drive (INF-1427) tomorrow.

Minimal network whitelist (control-plane only):
- TCP 9443: Redwood control-plane API (orchestration calls) - allow from Acme management CIDRs to Redwood control IPs in EU region
- TCP 9090: Health-check endpoint (optional; can be proxied to EU-only collector)
- TCP 9100: Metrics exporter (if enabled; otherwise we recommend disabling during activation)

APAC read-only opt-in options (pick one):
A) No BGP changes: use existing CDN/edge; configure Redwood to mirror read-only caches to APAC edge (no customer prefix announcements required).
B) BGP opt-in: customer announces additional /24 from colo to APAC for direct edge affinity (requires coordination with upstream providers).

Customer network tasks (minimal):
1) Whitelist TCP ports 9443 and 9090 from Redwood EU control IPs (list to follow).
2) Confirm whether you choose option A or B for APAC reads and document the chosen option in the runbook.
3) Prepare ACL toggle that can be flipped by your infra lead for the activation window (we'll provide a small script).

I'll attach the control IP list and the canary schedule in the runbook. Connor — please confirm we have permission to include the masked telemetry appendix Hannah recommended. Marissa / Steph — any objections to a 2-hour canary window + 24h observation?

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Site Reliability | Redwood Inference
Attachment stub: canary-schedule.txt (1kb)
